# Cognitive Load Theory — Briefing

## Executive Summary

Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) proposes that **working memory** is severely limited [1]. Instructional design should therefore minimise *extraneous* load [2].

### Key Concepts

*   **Intrinsic load** — inherent difficulty of the material
*   **Extraneous load** — imposed by poor presentation
*   **Germane load** — effort devoted to schema construction

| Type | Source | Can we change it? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intrinsic | The material | Only by sequencing |
| Extraneous | The design | Yes |

> "Working memory can hold about four elements." — Cowan, 2001

1. Present worked examples early
2. Fade guidance as expertise grows
3. Avoid split attention

See also [[Schema Theory]] and the `worked_example_effect`.
